subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: Which default recovery policy should OpenClaw use when an active session transcript is too large or repeatedly crashes during reload: quarantine/skip, automatic compaction-and-rotation, bounded truncation, or another explicit repair path?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but the permanent fix changes persisted session recovery behavior and could discard, archive, or hide user transcript state unless maintainers choose the product contract.

options.title: Quarantine before open
options.body: Detect pathological active transcripts before repair/open, move or mark them as degraded, and give users a doctor/fix path to recover or inspect the transcript.

options.title: Auto-compact and rotate
options.body: Run a bounded compaction/rotation recovery path before normal open so the active transcript shrinks while the old JSONL remains archived.

options.title: Bootstrap cap only
options.body: Land the open bootstrap marker circuit breaker as a partial mitigation and keep the broader transcript recovery behavior tracked here.

recommendation.title: Quarantine before open
recommendation.body: Detect pathological active transcripts before repair/open, move or mark them as degraded, and give users a doctor/fix path to recover or inspect the transcript.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame and recent session-manager repair work point to steipete as the best available owner for the persisted-session recovery contract decision.
